context.project: Obscura: Android camera app in Kotlin, Jetpack Compose and Camera2, built with Gradle. Target device is a Xiaomi 15T (Dimensity 8400, Android 16). There is a project skill `android-raw-camera` under `.claude/`.
context.scope: Portrait engine (`app/src/main/java/app/obscura/camera/depth/Bokeh.kt`), macro engine (`app/src/main/java/app/obscura/camera/depth/FocusStack.kt`), capture control (`app/src/main/java/app/obscura/camera/camera/CameraController.kt`), frame helpers (`app/src/main/java/app/obscura/camera/time/FrameOps.kt`). Offline tooling can go in `tools/` or `prototype/`.
context.desired-behavior: Macro produces images with measurably more depth of field than one frame. Portrait produces blur that matches a reference on objective measures and wins a blind comparison. Every change is justified by evidence captured on the device, not by synthetic tests.

research: Look up before task 1, from the named source: - Camera2 behavior of LENS_FOCUS_DISTANCE, LENS_STATE, LENS_INFO_FOCUS_DISTANCE_CALIBRATION and LENS_INFO_MINIMUM_FOCUS_DISTANCE, and how manual focus behaves on logical multi-camera devices (source: developer.android.com CaptureRequest, CaptureResult and CameraCharacteristics reference pages). - Whether a third-party app can read MediaTek VSDOF depth from a public stream (DEPTH16 or DEPTH_POINT_CLOUD, REQUEST_AVAILABLE_CAPABILITIES_DEPTH_OUTPUT, dynamic depth). Find what is documented about the vendor depth keys (source: Android camera depth docs and AOSP camera metadata docs; treat forum posts as unconfirmed). - The current stable version and API of ML Kit Subject Segmentation and MediaPipe image segmentation on Android, and whether each runs on-device without Play Services (source: developers.google.com ML Kit docs, ai.google.dev MediaPipe docs). - The method sections of Wadhwa et al. 2018, Barron and Poole 2016 (bilateral solver), He et al. (guided filter), and Burt–Adelson Laplacian-pyramid fusion (source: the papers themselves, arXiv or the publisher). Explore the codebase: - Read `Bokeh.kt`, `FocusStack.kt`, `CameraController.kt` and `FrameOps.kt` in full. Read their existing JVM tests. - Read the device probe output, wherever the repo stores it. Read the `android-raw-camera` skill under `.claude/`. - Record exactly which camera id, AF mode, AE and AWB lock state, and request keys the macro and portrait sweeps send today. Record pinned library versions with the date checked, and every source URL, in the plan before task 1.

task.name: audit-current-pipelines
task.description: Map what the code actually does, request by request and stage by stage, and list every point where real-device conditions differ from what the synthetic tests assume.
task.verification: - Every stage row in the plan cites a file:line that exists. For a sample of rows, confirm with `grep -n` on the cited symbol.

task.name: root-cause-hypotheses
task.description: Rank the likely causes of "macro does not work" and "portrait looks unnatural". For each one, name the captured evidence that would confirm or reject it.

example.input: Macro stack looks identical to a single frame.
example.output: Hypothesis H1: the lens did not move. Test: per-frame LENS_FOCUS_DISTANCE and LENS_STATE across the sweep, plus the physical camera id. Rejected if distances span ≥ 3 D with LENS_STATE stationary on every frame.
example.reasoning: If the lens never moved, no merge algorithm matters. This is the cheapest check and it gates everything after it, so it ranks first.

example.input: Portrait background blur has holes and sharp patches on walls.
example.output: Hypothesis: the Laplacian focus measure has no signal in textureless regions, and the fill propagates wrong depth into them. Test: overlay the dumped confidence map on the final image. Confirmed if the sharp patches match low-confidence pixels.
example.reasoning: This is an algorithmic limit of depth-from-focus, not a tuning issue. It points to a different depth source, not to new thresholds.

example.input: Glowing outline around the subject's hair.
example.output: Hypothesis: the quarter-resolution blur is composited without layer separation, so background blur leaks across the edge and the upsampling seam shows. Test: crop the edge region from the dumped CoC map and the composite.
example.reasoning: An edge halo can come from depth error or from rendering. The dumped CoC map tells them apart, and that decides which stage to fix.

task.verification: - Each hypothesis in the plan names a concrete metadata key or dump buffer from task 3.

task.name: capture-and-replay-spec
task.description: Specify the debug-dump capture mode and the offline replay harness that runs both pipelines on real captures.
task.verification: - The plan states the dump directory layout, the replay command line, and the parity tolerance as numbers.

task.name: redesign-both-engines
task.description: Commit to an algorithm design for each engine, in stages that are each testable against the replay harness.
task.requirements: - Order stages so the capture-correctness fixes come first and are measured before any merge or render change. - Give each stage its metric and its threshold from task 5.
task.verification: - Each stage in the plan maps to at least one hypothesis from task 2 and one metric from task 5.

task.name: evaluation-protocol
task.description: Define how the result is judged without relying on the user's or the agent's opinion.
task.requirements: - Macro passes when both hold: - the in-focus span on the 45° ruler is ≥ 3× the best single frame; - MTF50 at near, middle and far points is within 15% of the single frame focused there. - Portrait passes when both hold: - boundary F-score against a hand-labelled matte is ≥ the BOKEH-extension output on the same scene; - our output is preferred or tied in ≥ 60% of a blind randomized A/B against the BOKEH extension, with ≥ 5 raters who did not build it. - A frozen regression set of real dumps, with recorded metrics, is checked into the repo. Synthetic JVM tests stay, but they no longer count as evidence of quality.
task.verification: - Every threshold in the plan is a number with a stated measurement procedure.

execution.strategy: Sequential: 1 → 2 → 3, then 4 and 5 can be drafted in parallel. Keep the task checklist and research findings in `TASKS.md` alongside the plan, because older turns get summarized. Check any subagent's file:line citations before accepting them.
execution.constraints: - Ground every hypothesis and design choice in device metadata or a dumped buffer. "Tune the threshold" without device evidence is the failure that produced the current state. - Do not assume the vendor depth keys are usable. Mark VSDOF depth as conditional until research or a device dump shows a readable depth stream. - Keep the BOKEH extension path working. It is both a shipping engine and the comparison baseline.
execution.out-of-scope: - Changing app code in this run. This run produces a plan. - Other modes: selfie, double exposure, zoom burst, coach, gallery.
execution.stops: - If a step needs no input, keep going. Put status in the same message as the next action. - Stop only when blocked on the user: device captures and blind raters need them. Also stop before deleting data, force-pushing, or writing outside this repository. - Do not end the turn by asking whether to continue.
execution.escape: If a requirement is infeasible, name it once in the plan and continue with every part that is not blocked. Do not invent a workaround. For example: no adb access, RAW unavailable in the sweep configuration, or segmentation needing Play Services.

plan_mode_overlay: Read, search and propose only. Write the plan to `docs/depth-macro-plan.md` and the checklist to `TASKS.md`. Exit plan mode when the plan is complete.
check: Before reporting completion: - Run `git status --porcelain` and confirm only `docs/depth-macro-plan.md` and `TASKS.md` changed. - Re-read both files. Confirm there are no placeholders, every threshold is numeric, and every file:line citation resolves. - Report status for each original concern: macro, portrait blur, portrait depth, and the four expert questions. Mark each done / partial / skipped. - Write the user-facing summary in Hebrew. - Report: Blocked on me: the exact captures and raters needed from the user. Changed: Found: Unconfirmed: including where you looked, especially for VSDOF depth readability.
